faces.f:
"On every plane, there are those who run toward danger."
—Gideon Jura
"Wrath is no vice when inflicted upon the deserving."
"Many must die for the one who should not have perished."
If only every message were as perfect as its bearer.
"In memories, we can find our deepest reserves of strength."

"Even storm clouds bow to worship Avacyn."
—Elder Rimheit

"In the gathering there is strength for all who founder, renewal for all who languish, love for all who sing."
—*Song of All*, canto 642

"With his dream of unification fulfilled, Darien became the last king of Kjeldor. Those who followed were known as the kings of New Argive."
—*Kjeldor: Ice Civilization*
"The harder they try to extinguish my faith, the brighter it burns in the darkness."

"The tools of evil are mere things. And like all things, they cannot last forever."
—*Song of All*, canto 881
His prowess gives the guildless hope that they can hold out against tyranny.

"The battle is won. There's work to be done. / The Blessed Sleep must wait. / A fiend is about. It stalks the devout. / I'll save them from my fate."
—"The Good Geist's Vow"
Honor the gods of Theros, and they will return the favor.
The drums of war stir the hearts of all who fight for righteousness.
The Order of the Skyward Eye does the bidding of an evil force, unwittingly stirring fear and mistrust across Bant in accordance with his plans.
"Such a lord as this—all virtues' height—Had never been, nor ever was again."
"A river of lava is just another river to cross."
His watch ends only when he does.

"A boon from the angels should never be cast aside."
—Manfried Ulmach, Chief Inquisitor
The gods are fascinated by innocence, perhaps because it's a quality they themselves lack.
For the first time in his life, Grakk felt a little warm and fuzzy inside.
As Hedrax stepped into oblivion, he welcomed the unwavering silence.
"I am not afraid to die today nor afraid of what death will bring."
Skepticism fades in the face of the miraculous.
Some corpses the Golgari cannot claim. Some souls the Orzhov cannot shackle.

"One alone is fearsome; one among many is unstoppable."
—Benalish proverb
"Thraben is our home and I will not see it fall to this unhallowed horde."

"Guilds be damned. We can fend for ourselves."
—Vennick of the Gateless
There's no stronger armor than the bravery of those beside you.
Saltfield nomads call a sudden storm a "whitemane."

"I have seen and heard much here. There are secrets within secrets. Let me show you."
—Takara, to Eladamri
The wills of mortals shift as the tide ebbs and flows.
Nothing escapes a sharp mind.

"The Origin Query will wait. We must ensure we survive to return to it."
—Pelyus, vedalken ordinar
Kongming and Lu Su tricked Wei troops into shooting over 100,000 arrows at them to later use against the Wei at Red Cliffs.
Water calls to water, and the world is left exhausted and withered in its wake.

"She knows every step of this coastline, both above and below the surface, and she has hideouts all along the way. She will get you there."
—Jori En, expedition leader
All Mirri wanted to do was rest, but she couldn't ignore a nagging suspicion as she followed Crovax's skulking form.
"Of all the things that can be stolen, opportunity is the most valuable."

"Terrifying, but thankfully temporary."
—Teferi
No tactic transforms a battle like a well-timed carnivore.
When a strong mind moves, form and energy shift to heed it.
Going down with the ship is just the beginning.
In the final days before the disaster, all the crabs on Tolaria migrated from inlets, streams, and ponds back to the sea. No one took note.
"You can become anything if I just put my mind to it."

"Beauty to the eye does not always translate to the touch."
—Naimah, Femeref philosopher
Merfolk don't always know what they're looking for, but they're certain once they find it.
Even more than carrion, they crave the last words of the dying.
"There are no obstacles, only different paths."
Those who expect betrayal at every turn are seldom disappointed.

"You know it to be false, but when its claws find you, what you know won't matter much at all."
—Pol Jamaar, illusionist
Where the geometries of the world collapse, a master of the aether can harvest power beyond comprehending.

"Twice I have let the Legacy slip away. Never again."
—Karn, silver golem
Fblthp had always hated crowds.

"True strength is in the mind, for the body is too malleable a form."
—Politus, vedalken emisar
Knowledge demands sacrifice.
It returns eager to share the feast of blood and gore with its ghoulish master.
The spite of the Cabal turns meadow into mire.
Infested with vermin, ever hungering, dropping from night's sky.
"Brave scar or unfortunate tale? It all depends on your pain threshold."
Once they reached Orazca, the Legion's explorers ransacked tombs and temples, hunting for the Immortal Sun.
Their skills are extensive, and their appetite for battle just as vast.
"Why do you weep for the dead? I rejoice, for they have died for me."
"The rules are clear. If you want to leave, you need only convince another to take your place."
It feeds on dry bones in the sand and desperate pleas in the wind.
No mortal could atone for Ihsan's betrayal. Redemption required him to become something else.
Chainer's dark gift to a darker soul.

"No matter how busy my schedule gets, I always try to take time for that personal touch."
—Queen Marchesa

"The nezumi will do things for money no other thinking creature would consider. This, of course, makes them useful beyond words."
—Meloku the Clouded Mirror
Phyrexia wastes nothing. Its food chain is a spiraling cycle.

"Behold blessed perfection."
—Sheoldred, Whispering One

"The second wind of ascension is Reaver, slaying the unworthy."
—*Keld Triumphant*
An ogre's poisonous stench is like fine Kashkaval cheese to the noses lowest to the ground.
Opening Orazca unleashed more horrors than just the Immortal Sun.
They lived in different nations and fought in different eras, but as the Returned, they link arms as one.
The lamps on Wyndmoor Street snuff themselves at midnight and refuse to relight, afraid to illuminate what lies in the darkness.

"All are not equal—neither in life nor after death. Bontu's favorites will stand highest in eternity."
—Senifet, vizier of Bontu
The Cabal loves encores.
No matter how deep you bury it, some evil refuses to stay dead.
The lacerators cut themselves before each hunt. They must feed before the sun rises or bleed to death.

"On dark nights you can still see the light of the Vess girl's lantern out in the Caligo, seeking her lost brother. Those who follow are doomed to join her endless search."
—"The Fall of the House of Vess"

"The first birth celebrates life. The second birth mocks it."
—Mystic elder
"Eldrazi? Ha! Try walking through Zulaport at night with your pockets full. Now *that's* dangerous."

"Rage courses in every heart, yearning to betray its rational prison."
—Sarkhan Vol

"We earn no medals and fight for no titles. Blood is proof of our victory."
—Lovisa Coldeyes
The most frightening storms are those not woven by nature's hand.

"Even the threat of power has power."
—Jeska, warrior adept
Chandra never believed in using her "inside voice."
Any pyromancer can summon fire with a thought. The trick is putting it out.

"We wield the fires of rage. War is our blood and destruction our birthright."
—Crimson creed
Xenagos reveled while Theros burned.
If you stare at the sun for too long, you'll lose your ability to see clearly.
The upside to not thinking about the consequences is that you'll always surprise those who do.
Their eardrums may have given out, but the rest of them never will.

"Leave no scraps, lest you attract pests."
—Mardu threat

"You were once Mardu, so your body and will are strong. Now we must train your mind."
—Houn, Jeskai elder
A passionate recruiter will win a war before the first arrow flies.
The first morning after acquiring her familiar, the wizard awoke with fleabites and mange.
Hope of deliverance is scorched by the fire of futility.
The sparkmage shrieked, calling on the rage of the storms of his youth. To his surprise, the sky responded with a fierce energy he'd never thought to see again.
"Fate is not as fixed as you might think."
They'll attack whatever's in front of them—as long as you tell them where that is.

"The embers of our homes still smolder, and already the villages of Kjeldor burn in retaliation. What they have started, we will finish."
—Lovisa Coldeyes
Its growl is the crackling and popping of a wildfire untamed.
Nothing restrains a burning passion.

"It's rarely worth questioning where the mana comes from. Just be grateful."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage
Fire burns away both flesh and freedom.
When provoked, a flamekin's inner fire burns far hotter than any giant's forge.

"Proximity discouraged. Do not approach."
—Vulshok field guide
The sound of its plated tail beating on desert rocks is often mistaken for the footfalls of a much larger predator.
Keldon warriors don't need signals to tell them when to attack. They need signals to tell them when to stop.

"It's right to fear those that you keep locked away."
—Rahilda, Vildin-Pack alpha
"A hedron holds magic for a thousand years—or less, if need be."
Treefolk and elves share a common interest in the forests, but really the elves just feel at home with the view from above.
"I do not miss Jukai Forest. It is not my home. My home is Kamigawa, its people my family. Wherever I set my pack and rest my head, I am home."
If you feel the ground quake, run. If you hear its bellow, flee. If you see its teeth, it's too late.
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
A single seed unleashes a flurry of growth.

"From Gaea grew the world, and the world was silent. From Gaea grew the world's elves, and the world was silent no more."
—Elvish teaching

"Each night, the sun unravels and blows away. Each day, the spiders set a new one in the sky."
—Sunseeder myth
No matter the timeline, some legends will endure.

"Only the most effective tactics stand the test of time."
—Gamelen, Citanul elder

The kavu might be above you
—Llanowar expression meaning "keep an open mind"
In a withered world, the scent of healthy prey is enough to drive a predator to frenzy.
When it walked, it altered geography. When it bellowed, it changed the weather.
The best wishes include the will to tame their consequences.
The clamor of war ceased as both armies stood and marveled at the beauty of Gaea's work.
Though Shadowmoor's monster-haunted wilds beckon, she never leaves her post.

"Let nothing own the skies but the wind."
—Dejara, Giltwood druid
"Here lies Gond, hero of Safehold Taldwen. May he ever guide our quest."

"Meat *and* eggs. We eat!"
—Borborygmos
Hatred outlives the hateful.
"The thunder of hooves is music to my ears."

"The need for the pack is bred in their bones. Their true strength will not show itself for any other purpose."
—Garruk Wildspeaker
The executioner's tree in Thraben Cathedral holds the power to absolve more than the souls of the hanged.

"Life as we know it dangles on the brink of extinction. We must show the strength they would steal from us."
—*The Invokers' Tales*
Even among the hardiest warriors of the Temur, loxodons are respected for their adaptation to the mountain snows.

"Humans use pigs to hunt for mushrooms, don't they? It's like that."
—Harak, Malakir bloodwitch
While the smell of burning flesh is common in Grixis, the odor of smoldering brain matter is a rare treat.
Boggarts and disturbing bits of boggarts flew through the air with alarming and untidy regularity.
All the aether charts in the world can't compete with the trained eye of a talented scout.
After years of world-bending machinations, Bolas's triumph is at hand.
Tribal rivalries and petty disputes were laid aside at Eladamri's summons.
"I never thought I'd spend my life fighting. I'm a maker, not a destroyer."

"The enlightenment I never found in etherium I have found traced in the coatl's scales."
—Ranalus, vedalken heretic
Its fangs are in your flesh before its hiss leaves your ears.
Dominaria's most ancient evil.
"Yawgmoth," Freyalise whispered as she set the bomb, "now you will pay for your treachery."
Which is worse—the sleep which never ends or that which never comes?
The dwarves call their quicksilver techniques "improvisational weaponsmithing."
Only in Ravnica do the wolves watch the flock.
With their factories long destroyed, some of Mishra's creations still toil in remote areas, endlessly performing and reperforming their last orders.

"When I said I needed a hand, I didn't mean this."
—Gerrard Capashen
To Mirrodin, an explosive. To Phyrexia, a missionary.
"The explorer who found it got a bad deal when he sold it. He merely got rich."
The passing of the sai presages the end of the old clan and the ascent of the new.
It sees itself in all of its creations.
Its tines cannot be rung by mere physical force. Only magic of great power can start its eldritch resonance.

"Even if we defeat it, what remains to be saved?"
—Glissa Sunseeker

"There is great wisdom in rushing headlong into combat . . . if you're prepared."
—Kenjek, captain of the Thousand Swords
Travelers bathe in the falls to wash away curses from the pucas who lurk nearby.

"Do not linger in such places, child. There the gwyllions dance. If they find you, you will join in their revels for eternity."
—Talara, elvish safewright
At full moon, the river seeps over its banks and crawls through the woods like a blanket of serpents.
A ghoulcaller's playground.

"Center of the Sea, Eye of the World, Shrine of Enlightenment. Seek it for answers. Seek it for healing. Seek it and return transformed."
—Scroll fragment from the ruins of Minamo
The limbs of Pendelhaven extend as far as the meek roam, and reach as high as they strive.
Not all deaths are etched with mythic meaning and iconic glory.
Rishada is the gateway to free trade—but the key will cost you.
Hobs bury their kin far from home. They believe the dry, open ground keeps hags from stealing the bones and gwyllions from stealing the spirits.
As their roots soaked in a weak tea of bogwater and decay, the trees absorbed the essence of death into their living tissue.
Nothing lives within it, yet there is life.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
A spike and a maul are needed to crack their shells, but the taste is worth the effort.
The wurms become so big, a single scale can be used as a roof for a human dwelling.

faces.f: It can be a key, a weapon, and a way to attain great power.
The thieves of Venice are dependable allies of the Assassins, ready at any moment to cause a ruckus.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — You and target opponent each draw two cards.
II — Exile target artifact an opponent controls.
III — Each player chooses three nonland permanents they control. Destroy all other nonland permanents.

faces.f:
"Search the area! He can't have gone far!"
—Palazzo guard
"I went through hell to bring you here. It had better be worth it."

"Be my eyes, Senu!"
—Bayek of Siwa

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after IV.)
I, II, III — Mill three cards. You may put a historic card from among them into your hand. (Artifacts, legendaries, and Sagas are historic.)
IV — Historic spells you cast this turn cost {2} less to cast.

faces.f: The device can spy on anyone with just a drop of their blood.
History cannot be changed, and the Animus is not kind to those who try.
No mark remains hidden and no secret can be kept from an Assassin possessed of this unique gift.

"For a secret brotherhood, you certainly do get a lot of new recruits."
—Leonardo, to Ezio

"Who needs stealth when there's no one left to raise the alarm?"
—Jacob Frye
Just what the doctor ordered.
In the Animus, death is only a temporary setback.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Destroy target tapped creature an opponent controls.
II — Whenever an Assassin you control attacks this turn, put a +1/+1 counter on it.
III — Return target Assassin creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield with an additional +1/+1 counter on it.

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — This Saga deals 4 damage to any target.
II — Create two 1/1 black Assassin creature tokens with menace.
III — Whenever an Assassin you control attacks this turn, create a 1/1 black Assassin creature token with menace that's tapped and attacking.

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter.)
I — Exile a permanent card from your graveyard. You gain life equal to its mana value.
II — Put a number of +1/+1 counters on target creature you control equal to the mana value of the exiled card.
III — Return this Saga and the exiled card to their owner's hand.

faces.f: Not all glory is won with an axe.
"Ma cosa?! Shoot! Shoot the flying demon!"
"Until you have found a cause worth fighting for, you cannot know what you will sacrifice for it."
"The Creed is a warning. Ideals too easily give way to dogma. Dogma becomes fanaticism."
". . . and our blades shall never tire."
Haunted by memories he never had, of a family that was never his.
"Our will never rests . . ."

"What is a man but the sum of his memories? We are the stories we live! The tales we tell ourselves!"
—Clay Kaczmarek
"Know thy enemies as thy kin."
"My destiny is mine to weave."
"When I was a young man, I had liberty but I did not see it. I had time, but I did not know it. And I had love, but I did not feel it."

"Now you're ready to sail for the Horn,
Weigh, hey, roll and go!"
—"Randy Dandy Oh"

"Pirating might be seen as a man's life, but I guarantee: it's the most liberty a woman's going to find in this world."
—Anne Bonny
"I shall walk in the darkness and strike swiftly. No one will stop me in my hunt."
"Information is a weapon as potent as any Assassin's blade."
An Assassin's best armor is not being seen.
When the sun removes all shadows, the Assassins create their own.
The leap of faith is a sacred rite of the Assassins—it strengthens their resolve and purges fear from their hearts.
"We make history yours!"

"Monteriggioni will outlast her enemies."
—Mario Auditore
For the crime of trying to save her brother, Kassandra was thrown from Mount Taygetos—forced into exile with nothing but a broken spear and the will to survive.
The Hidden Ones were disciplined and patient, always waiting for the perfect moment to strike down their target and escape unnoticed.

"Requiescat in pace."
—Ezio Auditore

"Mighty kind of these fellows to keep our riches safe for us. Let's go thank 'em properly!"
—Edward "Blackbeard" Thatch

"So long as men retain free will, there can be no peace."
—Al Mualim, to Altaïr

"I do not wish to speak with you, but through you. You are the prophet. You've played your part."
—Minerva

"Those who don't stand with us, stand against us."
—Deimos
An Assassin has no weapon as deadly and no ally as dependable as the shroud of night.

"Then I leave you in the hands of fate."
—Ezio Auditore
Ratonhnhaké꞉ton's blade found its mark, putting an end to the desperate struggle between father and son.

"Before our final act, I would like to toast all you brave people who joined us tonight to celebrate life . . . and death."
—Maxwell Roth

"There have always been people who lust for power and control. And there have always been people who oppose them."
—Darius, to Kassandra

"We have done good."
—Aya of Alexandria

"A merry life and a short one, as promised. How well I know myself."
